items.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022
items.q: So I went there and the band consisted of an organ player named Tony Pasco.

ctx.x: What was the phone calls to home like?

Well it was tough. I’d talk to the kids, the other three kids were old enough to talk to me and my old lady and my youngest son was just a baby at the time. It was very difficult. And then this manager, this John Powell, you know at least now I was making $300 a week, I could send, you know $250 home through Western Union so she could pay the rent and buy some food. And it was really just stretching it out. And then John Powell said, “Hey, you’re packing the room, I’m going to ask for more money.” And then he…

Tony and the rest of the band was a drummer. So it was an organ and drums, and the drummer was the owner of the club, Perry Williams, who played drums once in a while. So opening night, as bad as it was, it was still better than where I was and so I was thanking God for that and I went out and I was singing some song to open, “The Lady is a Tramp” or something, to open the show. And halfway through the drums stopped. Well you know I’m in show business, I’m not going to turn around and say what happened to the…
